Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

I need to analyze the puzzle, which seems to involve a canvas background in color 2 along with several solid-colored shapes. I’m noticing some noise markers in colors 1, 7, and 8 embedded in there. It looks like the output keeps certain components while filtering out single pixels of noise. However, the scattered 7s might actually be parts of a shape. I need to preserve connected components and remove any unrelated pixels, ensuring that object 9 stays visible. I need to ensure that I submit the grid with the correct background, only removing certain isolated pixels. My last output was corrupted, so it's essential to use the last grid with overlays that correctly represent the object.

**Examining graph issues**

I might have a tiny mistake with the demo output that removes noise color and replaces it with a local base color. I need an actual mask grid and all noise for my tests on overlays and standalone markers.
